paper.title: Building Cooperative Embodied Agents Modularly with Large Language Models
paper.central_claim: CoELA, a cognitive-inspired modular LLM framework (perception, memory, communication, planning, execution), lets decentralized embodied agents plan, communicate and cooperate on long-horizon multi-objective tasks with costly communication; CoELA driven by GPT-4 surpasses strong planning-based baselines (more than 40% efficiency improvement) and shows emergent effective communication; a LoRA-tuned open LM (CoLLAMA) achieves promising performance; natural-language communication earns more human trust.
paper.claim_type_note: Paper also formalizes the setting and two environments and runs a user study; self-described central contribution is the CoELA framework (anchors v2 precedent 3).

signatures.object: Per-agent decision loop: Communication LLM drafts a message, Planning LLM picks one entry of a state-dependent Action List (including 'send message'), harness executor performs it.
signatures.information: Egocentric RGB-D -> fine-tuned Mask-RCNN -> semantic map/text state (task progress, self and other states), last K actions and D dialogues, received messages; partial observability; oracle-perception variant reported separately.
signatures.operation: Retrieve memory -> template to text -> LLM message generation 'in mind' -> LLM multiple-choice planning with zero-shot CoT -> high-level plan.
signatures.output: High-level plan index (go to room, explore, grasp, put, transport, send message).
signatures.conditions: Two decentralized agents (possibly human), broadcast noise-free messages that cost a step, 3000 frames (TDW-MAT) or 250 steps (C-WAH).
signatures.feedback: Next observation and incoming messages; no external checker of the chosen plan beyond list enumeration.
signatures.selection_rule: LLM chooses among enumerated options; no consensus/validator/rejection rule.
signatures.persistence: Within-episode semantic map, task progress and bounded action/dialogue history; Procedural memory never updated.
signatures.later_use: Re-injected into the next prompt of the same episode only.
signatures.claimed_effect: TR 0.71 (CoELA+CoELA) vs 0.61 (RHP+RHP) and 0.43 (RHP alone); C-WAH 57 vs 75 steps (symbolic obs), 92 vs 103 (visual obs).
signatures.failure_boundary: No 3D spatial info, unaware of low-level execution, counting/reasoning slips; communication gives no significant gain between AI agents.

signatures.object: Hard-coded perception/execution modules around the LLM (Mask-RCNN semantic mapping, A*-based procedural execution).
signatures.information: LLM sees only text; executor holds environment-specific procedures; perception supervised with GT masks from the simulator on training scenes.
signatures.operation: Execution module expands each high-level plan into primitive actions (A* navigation + rule-based interaction).
signatures.output: Primitive actions (move 0.5 m, turn, grasp, put, drop, send message).
signatures.claimed_effect: Removing the Execution module: trials 'struggle to finish any task'; removing Memory: steps nearly double.
signatures.failure_boundary: Reliability of executor assumed; no failure rates of the executor or perception propagated.

signatures.object: Open LM planner (LLaMA-2-13b-chat) tuned with LoRA on CoELA trajectories (CoLLAMA) to pilot the same harness.
signatures.information: Teacher: GPT-4 CoELA run in TDW-MAT training episodes; student sees the same prompts.
signatures.operation: Collect 2k trajectories from 10 training episodes, manually keep 572 with good communication/reasoning, LoRA fine-tune (30 epochs).
signatures.later_use: Replaces GPT-4 in the test-set rollouts.
signatures.claimed_effect: CoLLAMA 0.70 TR vs LLaMA-2 0.53 vs GPT-4 0.71 (single run).
signatures.failure_boundary: Single environment, offline teacher-visited states only, one run.

gap.author_gap: Cooperative embodied agents under decentralized control, raw sensory observations, costly natural-language communication and long-horizon multi-objective tasks; prior platforms neglect communication or use non-linguistic channels, and it is unclear whether LLMs can do distributed embodied cooperation.
gap.checked_gap: The problem definition (costly-communication multi-agent cooperation with raw observations) is concrete and sourced. The gap the method most needs to close -- that language communication improves AI-AI cooperation -- is not borne out by the paper's own ablation (no significant drop without communication).

gap.method_response: Five-module cognitive architecture; LLM used for message generation and plan selection; hand-written perception/execution.
gap.remaining_gap: Communication utility among AI agents, spatial grounding, low-level awareness, variance and cost evidence.

claims.text: CoELA (GPT-4) outperforms strong planning-based baselines (>40% efficiency improvement).
claims.setting: TDW-MAT 24 test episodes; C-WAH 10 test episodes; two agents.
claims.baseline_control: RHP/MHP hand-designed planners alone and in pairs; MAT given oracle inputs.
claims.selection_vs_test: Test episodes drawn from held-out floorplans for trained parts; prompt development set not disclosed.
claims.result_denominator: TR 0.71 (CoELA+CoELA) vs 0.61 (RHP+RHP) vs 0.43 (RHP alone); steps 57 vs 75 (MHP+MHP) vs 111 (MHP alone); CoELA 1 run, baselines 5 runs.
claims.allowed_conclusion: The >40% figure is cooperation EI relative to the solo baseline; versus the best cooperating baseline team the gain is about 16% relative TR / 24% fewer steps, from single runs on 24/10 episodes.

claims.text: Emergent effective communication improves cooperation; natural-language communication earns human trust.
claims.setting: Qualitative cases (Fig 3); ablation Fig 4c; 8 humans, 80 trials on C-WAH.
claims.baseline_control: CoELA w/o communication; MHP with template language.
claims.result_denominator: Trust 6.3 vs 4.7, p=0.0003; no significant AI-AI drop without communication.
claims.allowed_conclusion: Natural-language communication raises human-rated trust in C-WAH; its performance value among AI agents is not shown.

claims.text: A fine-tuned open LM (CoLLAMA) reaches competitive performance.
claims.baseline_control: GPT-4 and LLaMA-2 in the same harness.
claims.selection_vs_test: Training from 10 training episodes; test on held-out floorplans.
claims.allowed_conclusion: On one benchmark, a LoRA-tuned 13B model approaches GPT-4 within noise-unknown single-run differences.

assessment.evidence_level_reason: Closed-loop simulator-judged success in two environments; human trials; no real robot and no environment unused by design (transfer not met).
assessment.strongest_supported_claim: In two simulators and on small single-run test sets, an LLM-driven modular agent cooperating with itself or a rule-based partner completes more sub-goals/with fewer steps than the corresponding hand-designed teams; removing memory or the executor hurts; humans trust the language-communicating agent more; a LoRA-tuned 13B model approaches GPT-4 on TDW-MAT.
assessment.cannot_claim: That communication helps AI-AI cooperation, that the >40% figure is over the best baseline team, any robustness estimate, any cost advantage.
unresolved: K and D memory window sizes

G.reason: Concrete, sourced problem definition and environments with named baselines, but the premise that language communication is the missing ingredient is not borne out by the paper's own AI-AI ablation and the nearest LLM-agent neighbors are only discussed, not compared.

M.reason: Modules are justified (LLM weak at low-level control, ablation confirms) and the multiple-choice Action List is a sensible interface, but the communication module's contribution is unproven for AI-AI and several assumptions (reliable executor, perception, bounded window sizes) are thin.

X.reason: Information flow, prompt components and action space are reconstructable from the appendices; K/D, sampling seeds and executor rules are missing and no verifier/consensus exists; limitations are stated (3D spatial, low-level, reasoning).

measurement.reason: Simulator-computed TR/steps are trustworthy, but CoELA is one run on 24/10 episodes, no success rates or failure handling for unfinished episodes are given, perception-oracle and privileged-MAT variants mix, and the anchors v2 cap applies to single-run results.

causality.reason: One-at-a-time module ablations (memory, execution, backbone) exist but numbers are figure-only; headline comparison is against structurally different hand-designed planners; communication ablation contradicts the claimed value.

holdout.reason: Trained parts (Mask-RCNN, CoLLAMA) use training floorplans and the test set is separate, but the prompt/design development set is undisclosed, both environments were designed for, and GPT-4 contamination is unaddressed.

statistics.reason: CoELA single run, no variance, no CIs; only a t-test on human ratings; two qualitative failure examples and no failure decomposition.

cost.reason: Cost is mentioned only as the reason for single runs; communication step cost is counted in episode time but no calls/tokens/latency/dollars; no matched LLM-call budget for baselines.

status_reason: Complete html-full body plus appendices read; all eight ratings resolved; score computed mechanically.
